subject: Constella/Redwood: architecture & validation probe
messages:
From: Aisha Rao <aisha@constella.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Constella] Partner validation kickoff + architecture sketch

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking a look — Constella's delivery team is eager to run a short technical validation with Redwood to ensure our reference design will meet latency and security goals for our joint customers in the EU. I attached a top-level architecture diagram and a brief list of our functional constraints.

High level:
- We plan to call Redwood-hosted endpoints for generation and optionally use Dedicated for high-throughput tenants.
- We need VPC peering for Private deployments and HSM/KMS integration for keys.
- Expected peak concurrent sessions: ~1200 for tier-1 customers; median sequence length ~512 tokens.

Can we schedule a 60-minute architecture review + test-scope session next week? Our team will need:
- confirmation on model variant deployment options
- recommended batching and KV-cache settings for our workload
- a short smoke plan for validation (we can provide sample payloads)

Attachment(s): constella-arch-diagram.png (image/png)

Aisha Rao

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Constella] Partner validation kickoff + architecture sketch

Thanks Aisha — this looks straightforward and we can absolutely run a short validation. Proposed next steps:

1) Architecture review (60m) — goal: agree on reference topology and identify any redlines for private deployments.
2) Staging run (2 x 4h windows) — smoke traffic using your sample payloads to capture latency p50/p95 and token cost burn.
3) Security/compliance check — we will share a short safety checklist and SOC2 evidence summary up-front.

Initial technical checkpoints (we'll cover in the review):
- Model mapping: which open models you expect in production and tolerance for quantized variants.
- KV cache strategy: expected session reuse and recommendations for cache TTL.
- Batching targets: target latency SLOs vs batch sizes for Dedicated.
- Private deployment networking: VPC peering vs private link, IP whitelisting, and KMS integration pattern.

I've attached our Redwood safety checklist to this thread — it covers evidence we can share immediately. Sergio will drive the staging plan and operational runbook. Please propose two slots next week (we're in PDT) and we'll confirm.

Attachment(s): redwood-safety-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -0700

Aisha — quick note from the ops side on how I'd like to structure the staging run so we get actionable signals:

Planned smoke windows (we'll coordinate exact times):
- Window A (warmup): 30m low-rate traffic with high-session churn to validate KV behavior.
- Window B (load): 4h ramp to peak (target 1200 concurrent sessions) with two sustained plateaus to collect p50/p95 and GPU utilization.

Key measurements to capture:
- Token throughput and token-level cost by model variant
- p50/p95 latency for generator endpoints and tail behavior during bursts
- Batch sizes achieved and backlog/drop-rate if any
- KV hit ratio and memory pressure on Dedicated pools
- End-to-end auth latency (KMS sign/verify) for Private deployments

Deliverables from Redwood:
- A runbook (pre-run checklist + failover play) — I'll link a draft here: https://drive.redwood.com/s/constella-arch-8473
- Per-route dashboards we will populate (console links provided during run)

Reqs from Constella:
- representative payload set (50-200 samples)
- expected model list and target SLOs per customer tier

If that all looks good, Kimberly can coordinate calendar invites.

Sergio Alvarez
Principal Technical Ops | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
